attempted_derivation.blocking_gap: The branch still lacks certified values or analytic bounds for beta_v, r_v, D_v, and tau_tail in the actual locked hairpin endpoint geometry.
steps: Name of conceptual pressure: replace the abstract Wilson/OS obstruction by a finite same-theory endpoint sign interval for the connected R term after H,K are known.

Start from the regulated Wilson plaquette-sheet expansion and write endpoint contributions as source derivatives of log Z_v, so the manipulated object is a connected cumulant in the original heat-kernel theory.
Use the connected log to keep Wick-square contractions out of R_end; their earlier role is a positive Gram contribution and they are not a falsifier of the corrected second-order form.
Apply the null-channel incidence identity to the straight C_A f f contact. This leaves endpoint/corner cumulants as the only possible negative contribution.
In the small heat-kernel endpoint box, express the singlet fourth cumulant as kappa_v^sing=-beta_v+eps_v. Insert it into the pair weights 2,-4,-4 to get D_v=2G12-4G13-4G23.
Split D_v into [D_v]_+ and [-D_v]_+. Negative kappa_4 is dangerous only on [D_v]_+; equal or balanced endpoint boxes contribute to the protective side.
Package the result as the interval I_260 for M_G+R_end+tail. The hard gate is now finite endpoint source data plus a uniform tail estimate.
attempted_derivation.why_not_yet_a_proof: This is a regulator-level conditional certificate for one finite Wilson block. It does not prove OS positivity or the Clay target; it identifies the valid endpoint computation whose positive interval would promote this block and whose negative interval would be a concrete same-theory falsifier.

branch_outputs.branch_title: Post-H,K endpoint kappa_4 clipping certificate for reflected Wilson hairpins

assumptions: Model: four-dimensional Euclidean SU(N) Yang-Mills is regulated by heat-kernel plaquette weights on a reflection-positive lattice collar, with gauge-invariant Wilson plaquette sheets as the test algebra.
Regime: a<<ell_v<<delta and endpoint boxes B_v isolate corners of the reflected hairpin collars while keeping the bulk straight segments separated from the reflection plane.
Uniformity: the endpoint cumulant expansion has a cutoff-uniform fourth-order remainder and a tail bound summable over endpoint boxes before taking the continuum limit.
Cancellation assumption: connected-log subtraction removes Wick-square Gram terms, and the null incidence identity removes the straight C_A f f commutator contact on non-endpoint segments.
Sign-certification assumption: each singlet endpoint fourth cumulant admits an interval kappa_v^sing=-beta_v+eps_v with 0<=beta_low(v)<=beta_v<=beta_high(v) and |eps_v|<=r_v.
Same-theory assumption: source derivatives are evaluated in the same heat-kernel Wilson theory used for the collar OS matrix, not in an auxiliary boundary effective model.
definitions: source object: heat-kernel plaquette-sheet endpoint boxes B_v at cutoff a with local source partition functions Z_v(s) for singlet Wilson flux insertions X_{i,v}.
target object: the corrected post-H,K Schur-Feshbach null-channel scalar S_end for the same finite reflected Wilson block, not a redefined boundary theory.
controlled interface: connected fourth source derivatives of log Z_v mapped through the null-channel endpoint incidences D_v=2G12(v)-4G13(v)-4G23(v) after the safe contractions are removed.

same-theory condition: the endpoint boxes, Wilson renormalization, collar limit, and source probes are inherited from the locked gauge-invariant Wilson algebra without boundary counterterms or observable changes.
X_{i,v} is the plaquette-sheet boundary flux of hairpin i restricted to B_v, with orientation signs epsilon_i(p).
Gij(v) is the regulator-level geometric/color incidence pairing of the i and j endpoint footprints inside B_v after singlet projection.
C_N=(g^4/4)(T_F/N)^2 is the color prefactor left by the singlet Wilson expansion in the fundamental representation.

equations.label: endpoint source partition
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint box B_v is kept at positive lattice spacing and the heat-kernel plaquette-sheet regulator supplies a finite gauge-invariant local measure.

equations.label: singlet connected fourth cumulant
equations.valid_when: Valid when the Wilson flux sources are small and the singlet color projection is taken before the endpoint-box cutoff is removed.

equations.label: endpoint incidence dominance
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint footprints are represented by the same plaquette-sheet regulator and C_v is the local singlet incidence kernel after safe contractions.

equations.label: post-HK endpoint polarization
equations.latex: R_{\rm end}=C_N\sum_v \kappa_v^{\rm sing}D_v+T_{\rm corner},\qquad C_N={g^4\over4}\left({T_F\over N}\right)^2
equations.valid_when: Applies after diagonal Wilson factors, Wick-square Gram terms, and straight f f commutator contacts have been separated or cancelled in the null channel.

equations.label: clipped lower bound
equations.latex: \kappa_v^{\rm sing}=-\beta_v+\varepsilon_v,\ |\varepsilon_v|\le r_v\ \Longrightarrow\ R_{\rm end}\ge C_N\sum_v\{-\beta_{\rm high}(v)[D_v]_+ +\beta_{\rm low}(v)[-D_v]_+-r_v|D_v|\}-|T_{\rm corner}|
equations.valid_when: Valid when the certified cumulant interval is negative up to the stated error and the corner tail is bounded in the same regulator.

equations.label: promotion interval
equations.valid_when: Valid when M_G is the already computed positive Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin and tau_tail bounds all endpoint/corner remainder terms uniformly.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If a same-theory source computation gives D_v>0 endpoints with C_N beta_high(v) D_v plus tails exceeding the positive margin, the post-H,K finite block is demoted by a valid endpoint falsifier.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Turns the remaining connected boundary-OPE polarization R into a finite endpoint interval test. The hard gate is certification of beta_v, D_v, and tau_tail; success promotes the finite block, while failure gives a concrete falsifier interval.
candidate_lemmas.statement: In the locked three-hairpin finite block, after Wick-square positivity and straight f f contact cancellation, the post-H,K endpoint contribution is a clipped incidence sum. A negative compact-group fourth cumulant can demote the Schur-Feshbach scalar only at endpoint boxes with positive 12-dominance D_v>0; D_v<=0 boxes are protective up to certified same-theory remainders.

assumptions: The function F_v(t) is C^8 on |t|<=3h with a certified bound |F_v^{(8)}(t)|<=M8(v).
The source direction w_v is fixed by the endpoint incidence table and is not optimized after seeing the sign of the cumulant.
The finite-difference radius h is chosen so source perturbations remain inside the heat-kernel analytic neighborhood.
definitions: source object: the finite cutoff endpoint partition function Z_v(s) with sources coupled to the Wilson plaquette-sheet fluxes in B_v.
target object: a rigorous interval for the scalar singlet kappa_4 entering the post-H,K endpoint bound.
controlled interface: a central seven-point fourth-difference stencil applied to F_v(t)=log Z_v(t w_v), where w_v is the local null-incidence source direction.
same-theory condition: the seven source evaluations use the original heat-kernel plaquette action and the same Wilson sheet embedding as the OS collar block.

equations.label: seven point fourth derivative
equations.valid_when: Valid when F_v is evaluated at the seven symmetric source values in the same finite endpoint-box regulator.

equations.label: certified stencil error
equations.valid_when: Valid when an eighth-derivative supremum bound M8(v) holds throughout the closed interval from -3h to 3h.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If M8(v) grows too fast as a->0, the endpoint interval remains too wide and the finite block cannot be promoted.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Provides the numerical-analytic certification mechanism for beta_v and r_v in the endpoint clipping lemma.
candidate_lemmas.statement: The scalar endpoint fourth cumulant needed in L260 can be certified from seven same-theory evaluations of log Z_v along the null-incidence source direction, with an eighth-derivative error bound.

assumptions: The heat-kernel lattice measure satisfies a local cumulant decay or finite-volume cluster bound at the endpoint scale used in the collar construction.
Endpoint boxes are chosen with overlaps only where the Wilson hairpin geometry forces a corner contact.
All one-body Wilson renormalizations have already been removed by the Schur-Feshbach normalization and are not counted as tails.
definitions: source object: connected Wilson flux cumulants with at least one insertion outside the isolated endpoint boxes.
target object: a cutoff-uniform scalar tail bound tau_tail for the post-H,K null-channel interval.
controlled interface: cluster/locality estimates for heat-kernel plaquette-sheet cumulants outside endpoint boxes.
same-theory condition: the tail estimate is proved before changing regulators and survives the same collar cutoff-removal topology used for OS forms.

equations.label: tail domination target
equations.valid_when: Valid when the endpoint-box decomposition covers all forced corner contacts and the remaining cumulants obey the stated uniform locality estimate.

candidate_lemmas.failure_test: If tail terms are not uniformly smaller than the margin, the branch must quarantine the finite-block promotion even when local endpoint boxes look safe.
candidate_lemmas.proof_role: Separates a genuine endpoint falsifier from uncontrolled nonlocal remainder leakage.
candidate_lemmas.statement: Endpoint/corner tails can be quarantined from the main kappa_4 sign decision if their same-theory cumulant norm is smaller than the unused Schur-Feshbach margin after clipped endpoint contributions.

control_decision.pivot_test: Pivot or quarantine if the same-theory interval cannot be made cutoff-uniform, or if the lower endpoint is certified negative for an admissible 12-dominant hairpin geometry.
control_decision.promotion_test: Promote to proof delivery for this finite block if the certified lower endpoint of I_260 is strictly positive with regulator-uniform margins and the incidence table is realized by locked Wilson collars.
control_decision.reason: The branch is not looping. The hard gate is now endpoint source-derivative certification plus tail quarantine; success promotes the finite H,K block, failure produces a concrete post-H,K endpoint falsifier.

dependency_updates.description: Standard OS reflection-positivity closure transfers positive finite collar matrices; this move differs by computing the mixed connected Wilson endpoint cumulant that decides the post-H,K Schur-Feshbach scalar.
Standard Wilson perimeter, cusp, or one-body renormalization analysis does not decide the null-channel mixed endpoint kappa_4 because those factors cancel under the Schur-Feshbach normalization.
Compute or bound beta_v, r_v, D_v, and tau_tail for the locked endpoint geometry. Positive interval promotes the block; negative interval is a concrete falsifier.
Use timeline-definition-assumption-elicitor to verify that source objects, target scalar, same-theory condition, regulator, and non-claim boundaries remain explicit.

falsifiers: A certified source-derivative interval with D_v>0 dominance large enough that the lower endpoint of I_260 is negative is a direct post-H,K falsifier.
The heat-kernel eighth-derivative bound M8(v) may diverge so fast that kappa_v cannot be certified uniformly in the cutoff.
A corner tail with sign coherence in the null channel may exceed the clipped endpoint safety margin.
The compact-group fourth cumulant might fail to stay negative after the Wilson sheet source and singlet projection are imposed in the actual endpoint box.
A boundary counterterm or modified Wilson renormalization needed to define Z_v would violate the same-theory condition even if the interval were positive.

gedanken_experiment_design.expected_observation: For eta<=2 the negative compact-group kappa_4 is clipped into the protective or neutral side; only eta>2 can make D_v positive and create a possible negative interval. The stress case teaches whether a 12-dominant endpoint can defeat M_G before tails are considered.
held_fixed_controls: SU(N) heat-kernel plaquette regulator and singlet Wilson source normalization are fixed.
The previously computed H,K finite block and its Gaussian Schur-Feshbach margin M_G are held fixed.
No boundary counterterms, new Wilson renormalizations, or changes of the gauge-invariant test algebra are allowed.
Endpoint box size ell_v and collar separation delta remain in the same cutoff scaling regime.
gedanken_experiment_design.rationale: The branch needs a concrete endpoint dominance stress test, because the abstract obstruction has already been reduced to the sign of a finite R/kappa_4 interval.
gedanken_experiment_design.situation_seed: Asymmetric three-hairpin reflected Wilson collar with heat-kernel plaquette-sheet endpoint boxes: keep the 13 and 23 endpoint overlaps fixed while sliding the 12 pair footprints to increase their common endpoint incidence inside one box B_v.
gedanken_experiment_design.transfer_certificate_needed: A same-theory source-derivative certificate for kappa_v^sing, a cutoff-uniform tail bound, and a proof that the incidence deformation is realized by admissible reflected Wilson collars rather than by an auxiliary boundary model.
gedanken_experiment_design.varied_variable: The endpoint dominance ratio eta=G12(v)/(G13(v)+G23(v)) for the single stressed endpoint box.

branch_outputs.mathematical_learning: Cycle 260 attacks the conceptual pressure of making the last R/kappa_4 obstruction finite and sign-certifiable. The sharp value signal is that negative compact-group kappa_4 is not intrinsically dangerous; it is dangerous only through the clipped positive endpoint dominance D_v>0 after valid cancellations. This is route-changing at the branch scope: the proof state is no longer an OS/Wilson obstruction ladder but a finite same-theory endpoint interval computation with a clear promotion or falsifier outcome.
